'''Ingo Althöfer''' (born 1961){{r|born}} is a German mathematician and former professor of [[operations research]] at the [[University of Jena]].{{r|cos}}

Althöfer earned his PhD in 1986 at [[Bielefeld University]]. His dissertation, ''Asymptotic Properties of Certain Competition Systems in Artificial Intelligence and Ecology'', was supervised by [[Rudolf Ahlswede]].{{r|mg}}

==Contributions==
Topics in Althöfer's professional research include the realization of [[finite metric space]]s by [[shortest path problem|shortest path metrics]] in graphs and their approximation by [[Greedy geometric spanner|greedy spanners]],{{r|spanners}} [[algorithmic game theory]] and [[combinatorial game theory]],{{r|combgame}} and heuristic [[search algorithm]]s for optimization problems.

Althöfer is also known for his inventions of games and puzzles, including dice game [[EinStein würfelt nicht!]],{{r|bonvie}} for his experiments with [[self-assembly]] of [[Lego]] building blocks by running them through a [[washing machine]],{{r|lego}} and for his innovations in computer-human chess playing. In the 1990s he tested his "drei hirn" ["3-brains"] system, in which a human decides between the choices of two computer chess players, against strong human players including grandmaster [[David Bronstein]] and woman grandmaster [[Sofia Polgar]].{{r|drei}} In 2004 he and Timo Klaustermeyer introduced freestyle chess, a style of human chess playing allowing arbitrary consultation with computers or other people.{{r|cook}}

==Books==
* {{cite book | last1=Menzer | first1=Hartmut | last2=Althöfer | first2=Ingo | title=Zahlentheorie und Zahlenspiele: Sieben ausgewählte Themenstellungen. | publisher=De Gruyter | publication-place=Berlin/Boston | date=2014 | isbn=978-3-486-98963-2 | oclc=898769807 | language=de}}
* {{cite book | last1=Althöfer | first1=Ingo | last2=Voigt | first2=Roland | title=Spiele, Rätsel, Zahlen: faszinierendes zu Lasker-Mühle, Sudoku-Varianten, Havannah, EinStein würfelt nicht, Yavalath, 3-Hirn-Schach ... | publisher=Springer Spektrum | publication-place=Heidelberg | date=2014 | isbn=978-3-642-55301-1 | oclc=894170235 | language=de}}

He has also self-published other books through his personal publishing company, ''3-Hirn Verlag'', and is one of the editors of the multi-volume book series ''Rudolf Ahlswede's Lectures on Information Theory''.

* ''EinStein würfelt nicht!'' (2005)
* ''Galtoni'' (2012), a mixture of [[Connect Four]] and the [[Galton board]]
* ''San Jego'' (2015), a variant of [[Clobber]]
